Appointment of Non-Executive Director
Ampeak Energy is pleased to announce the appointment of Peter Parry as a Non-Executive Director of the Company, with immediate effect.
Mr Parry is an experienced board leader and non-executive director and long-serving magistrate. Across the private, social-housing and third sectors he has led business set-ups, restructuring, re-financing and investment. He co-founded and led FCG Vista Healthcare, one of the UK's larger independent healthcare providers, for 30 years before exiting in 2015. He is currently Independent Chair of Actif North Wales, the Regional Sport Partnership for North Wales. Mr Parry brings particular strength in financial oversight, risk and board effectiveness, and a commitment to organisations that create lasting value for shareholders and stakeholders, working constructively with executive teams.
Mr Parry has been nominated by SIMEC UK Energy Holding Limited ("SUEH") under the terms of the relationship agreement between the Company and SUEH, and is the second nominated director following the appointment to the board of Mark Dawber in July 2026. SUEH has a 29.6% interest in Ampeak and the ultimate beneficial owner of SUEH is Patrick Hughes.
Graham Reid, Ampeak Energy CEO, commented:
"On behalf of the Board, I look forward to welcoming Peter to the Board. Peter's depth of expertise will strengthen the Board as we execute on our strategy and capitalise on the opportunities ahead. We are confident his contributions will support the next phase of our growth."

latest.title: Ampeak Energy secures investment in AW1 project
latest.content:
1 Sep 2026 07:00
RNS Number : 7211S
Ampeak Energy Limited
01 September 2026
01 September 2026
AMPEAK ENERGY LIMITED
("Ampeak Energy" or the "Company")
Ampeak Energy secures investment in AW1 battery project
Ampeak Energy is pleased to announce that JBR Energy Holdings Ltd ("JB Energy"), a special purpose vehicle owned by various Directors of Jones Bros. Ruthin (Civil Engineering) Co. Limited ("Jones Bros"), our AW1 Battery Storage ("AW1") project construction partner, has made a strategic investment in the AW1 project at the Company's Uskmouth Sustainable Energy Park.
JB Energy has acquired a 24.7% equity stake in AW1 Storage Holdings Ltd ("ASH") from Ampeak Energy for £7.8m. The consideration comprises £3.9m for the acquisition of equity in the project's holding company and £3.9m for the purchase by JB Energy of a shareholder loan to AW1 Energy Storage Limited. Ampeak Energy remains the majority owner of the AW1 project holding company, ASH, with a 50.6% shareholding. One of the Directors of JB Energy is Huw Jones MBE, who is also the owner of Jones Bros.
This is a significant investment for the AW1 project, and the funds will accelerate the delivery of Ampeak Energy's existing development portfolio while also supporting exciting new opportunities the Company has been exploring in the UK and internationally.
Aligned with this objective to accelerate the build out of its development portfolio and as a condition of the sale, agreed with Cardiff Capital Region as part of its loan arrangement, Ampeak has committed that half of the funds raised are ringfenced for the delivery of the AW1 expansion project. This project is making excellent progress towards financial close and will see AW1 move from a capacity of 240MWh to 480MWh. This pre-commitment of funds represents a large portion of Ampeak's equity investment in this expansion, which is expected to reach financial close next year after the Commercial Operation Date of the first phase.
The investment also underpins Ampeak Energy's assumptions around the value of its portfolio of projects, with a value of £260,000/MW.
Jones Bros already serves as the principal contractor on the AW1 project, responsible for delivering the balance of plant and electrical works, which are progressing on schedule and on budget.
The investment is also a positive development for Wales and the local area, as Jones Bros gains greater visibility and participation in a broader pipeline of projects, so it can continue to offer more job opportunities. At its peak, the Uskmouth site had over 500 contractors and staff working across its multiple projects.
Graham Reid, Ampeak Energy CEO, commented:
"We are delighted to welcome the owners of Jones Bros as equity partners in our flagship AW1 project and would like to thank all those involved in making this happen. This investment is great for the project, great for our existing pipeline of projects, and great news for our shareholders as it will provide the funds to take our extensive knowledge and experience to develop new projects."
Huw Jones MBE, Jones Bros and a Director of JB Energy, commented:
"The AW1 project is a true flagship of regeneration, and we are delighted to be joining one of the leading companies delivering battery projects. As a Welsh-based company, we are proud to be helping deliver one of the largest battery storage sites in Wales."

596/2014, as it forms part of United Kingdom domestic law by virtue of the European Union (Withdrawal) Act 2018, as amended, and has been announced in accordance with the Company's obligations under Article 17 of that Regulation.

latest.content:

AMPEAK ENERGY LIMITED
("Ampeak Energy" "Ampeak" or the "Company")
Notice of Annual General Meeting
and
Ampeak Energy proposed Board appointments
Ampeak Energy announces that it has today made available to shareholders the Notice of 2026 Annual General Meeting ("AGM") and the Form of Proxy.
The Notice of AGM is available to view on the Company's website
here
.
Printed copies of the Notice of AGM and the Form of Proxy are being mailed or made available to shareholders, in line with shareholder communication preferences.
The AGM will be held at 11am on Monday, 13 July 2026 at the offices of Ashurst LLP, London Fruit & Wool Exchange, 1 Duval Square, London, E1 6PW.
Proposed Board appointments
Following the announcement early this year that Patrick Hughes had become Ampeak's largest shareholder, management have engaged with Patrick Hughes and his team, and the Company is pleased to announce the proposed appointments of two members of Patrick's senior leadership team to the Ampeak Board as Non-Executive Directors.
It is intended that Scott Martin and Mark Dawber (biographies below) will be joining the Ampeak Board following the conclusion of the Company's AGM. They bring significant experience in the energy and technology space and will help support the Company as it continues to deliver against its goals.
The proposed appointees have been nominated by SIMEC UK Energy Holding Limited ("SUEH") under the terms of the Relationship Agreement between the Company and SUEH. SUEH has a 29.6% interest in Ampeak and the ultimate beneficial owner of SUEH is Patrick Hughes.
In addition, David Taaffe, current Ampeak Chief Operating Officer, has also been nominated to join the Board, bringing a wealth of experience and a track record of delivery. It is intended that David will join the Board following conclusion of the AGM.
David Taaffe
David was appointed Chief Operating Officer in June 2022, having previously been responsible for project development and delivery since joining Ampeak in 2011. David holds responsibility for Ampeak's project portfolio, including the origination, strategic development and project financing of the Company's significant portfolio of Battery Storage projects. In recent years, David has been instrumental in achieving financial close of the AW1 Battery Storage project and establishing Ampeak's pipeline of a further 4.3GWh of Battery Storage development projects.
Prior to joining Ampeak, David worked for a number of international consultancies and developers and successfully delivered large scale energy projects in Ireland, UK, and New Zealand. David has a BEng (Hons) in Electrical Engineering from University College Dublin.
Mark Dawber
Mark Dawber is currently Managing Director of Valencia Energy, a privately owned UK renewable energy generation portfolio, where he holds full accountability for the business, all operations, energy trading, and the development of new projects.
Alongside this, Mark is Co-founder and Chief Energy and Infrastructure Officer of Era4, leading Energy Strategy, site development and delivery for sovereign AI infrastructure.
Mark brings deep operational expertise across the UK power sector, with a track record in technology development and deployment, reciprocating gas engine projects, behind the meter generation, PPA origination and energy trading.
Prior to Valencia, Mark spent over a decade at Viridor across operational, engineering and senior leadership roles, including Head of Power Generation for the national landfill gas estate, where he led a step change in availability, compliance and commercial performance across the portfolio.
Mark is a Chartered Fellow of the Chartered Management Institute (CMgr FCMI) and holds an MBA from Cranfield University and a BEng in Mechanical Engineering from the University of Southampton.
Scott Martin
Scott Martin is currently Group CFO of Patrick Hughes' family office, overseeing Mr Hughes' interests in companies across a variety of interests, including waste management, power generation, AI infrastructure and real estate.
Prior to this, Scott spent around four years as Finance Director of another family office advising on a portfolio spanning private equity, hedge funds, real estate, public equities and fixed income. He trained with PwC in London within the Asset and Wealth Management practice.
Scott is a Chartered Accountant (ACA) and holds a First Class Honours degree in Accounting and Finance from the University of Strathclyde.
Graham Reid, Ampeak Energy CEO, commented:
"On behalf of the Board, I look forward to welcoming Scott and Mark to the Board alongside David. Their depth of expertise and industry knowledge will significantly strengthen the Board as we execute on our strategy and capitalise on the opportunities ahead. We are confident their contributions will support the next phase of our growth."

company_30s.what_they_do: Ampeak Energy builds and operates offshore wind farms and battery storage projects in the UK.  Their main products are the MW‑scale wind turbines, on‑shore and offshore grid connections, and large‑scale lithium‑ion batteries that smooth supply for renewable generation.
company_30s.why_they_matter: The UK’s net‑zero target pushes demand for offshore wind, and battery storage is the missing piece that lets wind be a reliable baseload source.  Ampeak’s projects sit in the North Sea, a high‑potential area where the government is offering subsidies and the grid is expanding, giving the company a clear path to scale.
company_30s.current_state: The firm is past the idea stage and is now in the execution phase, having secured planning permission for AW2 and completed key offshore works for MeyGen.  It remains cash‑burning but has recently closed a funding round that should support construction and early operations.  The share price is currently trading near zero, reflecting the deep discount investors have applied to the company’s high‑risk, long‑term upside.

rns_narrative: Ampeak has been busy turning permits into concrete work: the AW2 battery project received formal planning, and the MeyGen offshore works are finished.  At the same time the company has been filing annual and AGM reports that show a steady burn but also a growing debt‑to‑equity ratio.
The second cluster of news is about financing and governance: major holdings were disclosed in February, and the company announced a new investor day in November to attract additional capital.
The final theme is operational progress: the company is moving from paperwork to physical construction, which is the most critical step for any renewable developer.

crowd_tape.dominant_theme: Quiet optimism around project milestones, but no real chatter yet.
crowd_tape.bull_narrative: Bulls are pointing to the completed offshore works and the new battery permit as proof that the company can deliver on its roadmap.
crowd_tape.bear_narrative: Bears warn that the projects still face regulatory hurdles and that the cash burn could outpace funding, putting the company in a fragile position if the market turns.
crowd_tape.sentiment_shift: The community has been largely silent; however, the latest investor day has sparked a slight uptick in discussion, hinting that a catalyst might be on the horizon.

whats_happening_now.attention_check: Google Trends is flat – no recent search interest, which means any positive news will catch the market by surprise.

near_term_catalysts: Completion of the AW2 battery construction and the start of commercial operation (expected Q3 2027).
A formal financing package that covers the remaining construction costs, announced at the next investor day.
Regulatory clearance for the final stages of the MeyGen offshore project, which would unlock a new revenue stream.
A significant uptick in wind power demand driven by the UK’s net‑zero policy, which could push the price of electricity higher and improve project economics.
expect_next.watch_for: Look for a sharp increase in trading volume (≥3× daily average) coupled with a bounce above the 20‑day moving average.  A positive earnings release or a new financing agreement would be a clear confirmation.  A delay or downgrade from a major regulator would be a red flag.
expect_next.timing_regime: The company appears to be in the early stages of the recovery cycle – the capital‑intensive phase is still underway.  A mean‑reversion bounce is likely only once the first commercial revenue stream starts, so patience is required.

buy_vs_sell.bull_case: If Ampeak’s projects hit commercial status, the stock could climb to 50% of its pre‑crash valuation, which would double the current price.  Historically, a green‑color deep crash bottom has delivered ~40% average returns; a RED+PURPLE combo would push that to over 100%.  The asymmetry is clear – the upside potential far outweighs the modest downside risk of a further decline to the current level.
buy_vs_sell.bear_case: The biggest risk is execution failure – if the battery or offshore projects stall, the company could run out of cash before generating revenue, pushing the share price to zero.  A realistic worst‑case scenario is a 90% decline from the current level, which would wipe out most equity holders.
buy_vs_sell.risk_reward: Potential upside: 2–3× current price if projects go live.  Potential downside: 1× current price if the company fails to secure financing or hits regulatory roadblocks.  The reward-to‑risk ratio is therefore roughly 2:1, making this a classic contrarian play.

playbook.if_bullish: Enter when the price breaks above the 20‑day moving average with volume at least 2× the average, indicating a new trend.  Position size should be limited to 5% of discretionary capital, with a stop 10% below the entry to protect against a false breakout.
playbook.if_watching: Wait for the first commercial revenue announcement or a new financing deal.  A price move to the 50‑day moving average with volume surging would be a clear trigger.
playbook.if_passing: None – there are no imminent delisting or bankruptcy signals.  The company’s projects are still in progress and the market has not yet punished it for any fraud or misstatement.

ai_insights.bottom_line: Ampeak Energy is a deep‑crash play that could double the price once its offshore and battery projects become operational, but the upside hinges on a successful funding round and regulatory clearance.
